matches.note: R1 identifies that the Jasypt password is reverse(busId+version) from plaintext columns of the same row, so anyone who can read the row can decrypt the key and forge JWTs.

unmatched_reported.note: fetchSecret ignores EntityStatus, so a JWT secret marked INACTIVE is still used to sign and verify tokens; that is a concrete revocation gap.
Caching the key for the life of the process is the deliberate design, and the multi-node divergence it describes needs out-of-band row changes, so it is speculative.
The race is benign and only causes redundant identical queries at startup, as the finding itself admits.
fetchSecret never decrypts, so the documented fail-fast on a corrupt row cannot fire and the failure is pushed to every request as DECR_ERROR.
Map.of rejects null values, so null busId/version throws a raw NPE before the intended BLANK_* SecException validation runs.
The per-request PBE cost is unquantified, and the finding itself asks for profiling to confirm it.
The finding says it is latent and that no caller of getKey was found.
An IPv6 ULA edge case and a DNS TOCTOU in a local-dev guard are minor and have no concrete security impact.
